lines: Q: What's the hardest part of meals for you? Or something else.
A: Jain food every day without repeating, and Ba's early dinner timing.

Q: Which apps do you order groceries on: Zepto, Blinkit, Instamart, BigBasket or Amazon? If you sign me in, I'll read your past orders to learn what your home buys and how often, so the plan and the shopping list fit you from the first week, and I can fill the cart for you. Nothing is ordered without your yes.
A: BigBasket for monthly, Zepto for daily. And later on the sign-in.
Q: Which is your main app, and which do you use when something isn't there?
A: BigBasket for monthly, Zepto for daily. If something's missing I check the other one.
Q: I have Hitesh (48), Bhavna (46), Dhruv (17) and Kantaben (76) eating at home. Anyone else who eats at home, or anyone who doesn't?
A: That's all four of us. No one else.
Q: Ramila cooks daily: Breakfast and Lunch at 8am. Is that right, and does the cook come for any other meals?
A: Yes, Ramila comes 8am daily, makes breakfast and lunch. No other meals from her.
Q: Is the cook short of time, say off to the next house, so only a dish or two in the morning?
A: No, she has about two hours, no rush.
Q: The cook comes every day: is food cooked at home all seven days?
A: Yes, Ramila comes all seven days, only mornings. Bhavna makes dinner every night. One night a week we eat out.
Q: What did the children have for breakfast over the past week? Tell me in as much detail as you can.
A: Dhruv is 17, not a child. He had thepla, khakhra, poha and dhokla on Sunday.
A: That's all I remember from last week.
Q: The children's lunch over the past week, or their school tiffin?
A: Dhruv eats lunch at home after school, same as us.
A: No school tiffin.
Q: The children's dinner over the past week?
A: Dhruv is the only child, 17. He eats what we eat for dinner.
Q: What did the adults have for breakfast over the past week? Tell me in as much detail as you can.
A: Same as Dhruv's breakfast — thepla, khakhra, poha, dhokla on Sunday.
A: No onion or potato in the poha.
Q: The adults' lunch over the past week?
A: Rotli, dal, bhaat and one shaak — tindora, bhindi or cabbage. Kadhi sometimes instead of dal. Dal dhokli on Sunday.
Q: The adults' dinner over the past week?
A: Khichdi and kadhi twice, other nights bhakri or thepla with a shaak. Ba ate before sunset, her own thing.
Q: Is anyone on a diet? High protein, low carb, diabetic, anything a doctor asked for.
A: Yes, I have high cholesterol, so less oil for me. Nobody else.
Q: Do the elders eat anything differently from the rest: less salt, softer food, no onion or garlic, a fasting day?
A: Ba doesn't eat green vegetables on ashtami and chaudas. That's it.
Q: Any food rules for the house? Veg, egg or non-veg days, fasting days, allergies, a dish someone won't touch.
A: We're Jain — no onion, no garlic, no potato or root veg, no eggs, no meat. Ba skips green veg on ashtami and chaudas.
Q: How often do you order in, and on which days?
A: We never order in. Saturday dinner we go out to a Jain restaurant.
A: sorry, it's Sunday dinner we eat out, not Saturday
Q: Does anything come on a subscription, like Country Delight or a milkman?
A: Amul milk, 2 litres every morning. That's it.
